title: Latent collateral counts toward the peg reserve only if conversion is automated, verifiable and under fifteen minutes
content:
A.3.3.2.2.1 splits ASC into Resting and Latent. Latent ASC (A.3.3.2.2.1.2) is Cash Stablecoins that are deployed elsewhere — in lending protocols, DEX liquidity, or liquid staking derivatives of stablecoins — and it counts toward the requirement only if three conditions hold:

1. "The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles";
2. convertible into Resting ASC "within 15 minutes under normal market conditions"; and
3. "The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and **triggered automatically** when ASC falls below specified levels."

The third condition is the one that carries the design. Liquidity that depends on a human noticing and acting is not liquidity during the fifteen minutes that matter; requiring pre-built automation with an automatic trigger converts a claim about theoretical convertibility into deployed infrastructure. An Agent cannot count an asset as latent reserve merely because it *could* be sold quickly — the selling machinery must already exist and must fire without instruction.

The framing is a useful general one: liquidity is treated as a property of the *conversion path*, not of the asset. The same USDC counts differently depending on whether an automated withdrawal-and-deposit route has been built for it.

A.3.3.2.2.1.2.2 caps Latent ASC at 25% of total ASC, so at least three quarters of the reserve must be resting bids already in the market. Automation reduces the delay but does not eliminate it, and "under normal market conditions" is exactly the qualifier that fails during a peg event — lending protocol utilization spikes and DEX depth evaporates precisely when the conversion is needed.

A.3.3.2.2.1.2.1 keeps discretion in reserve: the Core Executor Agents, consulting the Core Council Risk Advisor, "may impose limitations on the size of exposures to these protocols or to specific pools" that qualify as Latent ASC — a concentration control layered on top of the eligibility test.
description: Cash Stablecoins in lending markets or DEX pools qualify if convertible to resting support within 15 minutes by a fully automated process auto-triggered on ASC shortfall, capped at 25% of ASC.
